mainTopic: Who counts as a בכור: the בן חלל, a son of uncertain fatherhood, miscarriages, and a caesarean birth
overview: The amud opens with an argument about a בן חלל, the son of a כהן and a גרושה, whose כהן father died before redeeming him. The גמרא explains that if the father died after thirty days, everyone agrees the son is exempt. If the father died within thirty days, רב חסדא obligates the son, and רבה בר רב הונא exempts him because he stands in his father's place. A challenge from a pregnant convert is answered: a גוי has no legal lineage. ריש לקיש then rules like רב חסדא. Next, the גמרא discusses a son of uncertain fatherhood born to a widow who remarried within three months. רבי ירמיה explains that the son born after him loses the double portion. The גמרא adds, citing רבי ינאי, that a הרשאה cannot help sons who were never identified. Finally, a new משנה teaches which miscarriages do not cancel firstborn status. It then records the dispute between תנא קמא and רבי שמעון about a caesarean baby and the child after him, and the גמרא explains the פסוקים and reasoning behind each side.

steps.title: The dispute about a חלל son whose כהן father died
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the בן חלל must redeem himself. רבה בר רב הונא says he does not have to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A כהן died and left a son who is a חלל. רב חסדא says the son must redeem himself. רבה בר רב הונא says he does not have to redeem himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new argument between two אמוראים. The case is a כהן who died and left a firstborn son who is a חלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל is not a כהן, so as a firstborn he normally needs פדיון הבן. His father was a כהן, though, and could have kept the redemption money for himself. Now the father is dead. Does the son owe five סלעים to some other כהן, or not?

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
A priest
Son of a כהן from a forbidden marriage (such as to a גרושה); he does not have כהונה
To redeem himself (pay the five סלעים of פדיון הבן on his own behalf)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the son is a כהן just because his father was one. A חלל loses כהונה. That is exactly why there is any question about פדיון here.

phrases.english: It was stated: a priest who died
phrases.notes: Implied: he had married a divorcée.

phrases.english: and left a son who is a ḥalal
Rav Ḥisda said:
the son is obligated to redeem himself.
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
he is not obligated to redeem himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: כֹּהֵן שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ בֵּן חָלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא: the בן חלל must redeem himself. רבה בר רב הונא: he is exempt.

steps.title: If the father died after thirty days, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: If the father died after the thirtieth day, all agree the son is exempt, because the father already 'acquired' the redemption money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever the father died after thirty days, everyone agrees the son does not have to redeem himself, because his father already acquired the redemption money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument. It removes one case from the dispute, where the father died after thirty days, and says everyone agrees on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On day thirty, the obligation of פדיון falls on the father. Since he is a כהן, it is as if he gave the five סלעים and took them back for himself. The מצוה is already finished, so nothing is left for the son to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; there is no dispute here
Thirty days, when the obligation of פדיון הבן takes effect
His father acquired his redemption money
Where / in a case that

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּמֵת הָאָב לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: In any case where the father died after thirty days,
everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין הַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: that the son is not obligated to redeem himself,
since his father already acquired his redemption money.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּמֵת הָאָב לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the dispute in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father died after thirty days: the son is exempt according to everyone.

steps.title: The real dispute: father died within thirty days, and רב חסדא's reason
steps.stepSummary: The argument is only when the father died before day thirty. רב חסדא obligates the son because the father never acquired the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue where the father died within thirty days. רב חסדא says the son must redeem himself, because his father never acquired the redemption money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now says exactly where the two אמוראים disagree. It then gives רב חסדא's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father died before day thirty, the obligation never fell on him. So he never 'took' the money for himself. According to רב חסדא, the obligation now falls on the son, who is not a כהן, so he must pay a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they do disagree
Within (before the end of)

phrases.english: When they disagree is where
the father died within thirty days.
Rav Ḥisda says:
the son is obligated to redeem himself,
since his father did not acquire his redemption money.
phrases.notes: Text correction: לפדיונו emended to בפדיונו.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי הֵיכָא דְּמֵת הָאָב בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the case still in dispute after step 2, and explains רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father died within thirty days: according to רב חסדא, the son must redeem himself because the father never acquired the money.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא's reason: the son stands in his father's place
steps.stepSummary: The son can tell the כהן: 'I come with the power of a man (my כהן father) you could not have sued.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא says the son does not have to redeem himself. He can say to the כהן: 'I come with the strength of a man you could not have taken to court.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבה בר רב הונא's side. The son 'inherits' his father's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the father lived, no כהן could have demanded money from him, because he was a כהן himself. The son steps into his father's shoes and keeps that same protection. So even before day thirty, no כהן can collect from him.

keyTerms.meaning: I come with the power of (I stand in the place of)
A man (here: the father)
To bring a legal claim against

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: within thirty days, the son pays, since the father never acquired the money. רבה בר רב הונא: the son is exempt, because he stands in his כהן father's place.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna says:
the son is not obligated to redeem himself,
because he can say to him (the priest):
I come with the power of a man
against whom you could not bring a legal claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתֵינָא מִכֹּחַ גַּבְרָא דְּלָא מָצֵית לְאִשְׁתַּעוֹיֵי דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning to רב חסדא in the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father died within thirty days: according to רבה בר רב הונא, the son is exempt by claiming his father's power.

steps.title: Challenge from the pregnant convert
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a child born to a woman who converted while pregnant must be redeemed. Why can't he also say 'I come with my father's power,' since his father was a גוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if a woman converted while pregnant, her son is a בכור who must be redeemed for a כהן. But why? Let him say: 'I come with the power of a man (a גוי) you could not have taken to court!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר רב הונא's reasoning using a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי father has no obligation of פדיון, so no כהן could ever have sued him. By רבה בר רב הונא's logic, the son should inherit that exemption. Yet the משנה obligates him, so the logic seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
She converted while pregnant
A firstborn who must be redeemed by giving to a כהן
But why?

phrases.english: We learned: if she converted while pregnant —
he is a firstborn for the priest (must be redeemed).
But why? Let him say to him:
I come with the power of a man
against whom you could not bring a legal claim!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נִתְגַּיְּירָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת — בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן, וְאַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's principle of 'אתינא מכח'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The son of a גוי could make the same claim, since his father was never obligated. Yet the משנה obligates him.

steps.title: A גוי has no legal lineage
steps.stepSummary: A גוי is different: halachically he has no lineage, so the son cannot claim to stand in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גוי is different, because he has no lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה בר רב הונא by showing the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Standing in my father's power' only works if halacha treats you as his son. A convert's child is not legally connected to his גוי father. The חלל, however, is fully his כהן father's son and heir.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
A non-Jew
Lineage / legal family connection

phrases.english: A gentile is different,
as he has no lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any son could claim the exemption of a father who could not be sued.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a son legally connected to his father can step into his father's power. A גוי's son is not.
steps.whatToRemember: The principle 'I come with my father's power' works only when halacha recognizes the father-son connection.

steps.title: ריש לקיש rules like רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says: if the father died within thirty days, the son must redeem himself. If after thirty days, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון יאסיניא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: A כהן who died within thirty days and left a son who is a חלל: the son must redeem himself, because the father did not acquire the redemption money. If he died after thirty days, the son does not need to redeem himself, because the father already acquired the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement from ריש לקיש that matches רב חסדא's view exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש divides the cases by day thirty, just as the גמרא explained in steps 2 and 3. Within thirty days, the son pays. After thirty days, the son is exempt. This supports רב חסדא and rejects רבה בר רב הונא's idea that the son inherits his father's exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who transmits the teaching
ריש לקיש, the source of the ruling
Chain of transmission: X said in the name of Y

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש agrees with רב חסדא. The key date is day thirty: that is when the father 'acquires' the money for himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: ריש לקיש, a leading early אמורא of ארץ ישראל, sides with רב חסדא. This strengthens רב חסדא's position in the dispute.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Yasinia said,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
A priest who died within thirty days
and left a son who is a ḥalal —
the son is obligated to redeem himself,
since the father did not acquire his redemption money.
If he died after thirty days —
the son is not obligated to redeem himself,
since the father already acquired his redemption money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן יָאסִינְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main dispute and brings an authority who agrees with רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father died within thirty days: the son pays. Father died after thirty days: the son is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש via רבי שמעון יאסיניא

steps.title: Quoting the next case: a widow who remarried within three months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a woman who remarried within three months of her husband's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, a woman who did not wait three months after her husband died, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new case from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line for the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman remarried quickly and gave birth. Nobody knows whether this was a nine-month baby from the first husband or a seven-month baby from the second husband. The full משנה rules that this son is a בכור for פדיון הבן from the כהן, but not a בכור for inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: She waited
Her husband
Three months, the waiting period that makes it clear who the father is
Etc.; the rest of the quoted text is understood

phrases.english: And likewise, one who did not wait
after her husband three months, etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה continues: he is a firstborn for the כהן but not a firstborn for inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁהֲתָה אַחֲרֵי בַּעְלָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of a father who died within thirty days to a new case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son of uncertain fatherhood, born to a widow who remarried within three months, is a בכור for the כהן but not a בכור for inheritance.

steps.title: How can the son of uncertain fatherhood inherit anything at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the son gets a regular share, then asks how, since the heirs of each husband can push him away.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only as a firstborn for inheritance that he does not count, but he does take a share like an ordinary son. But why? Let him go to the heirs of this husband, and they will push him away. Let him go to the heirs of that husband, and they will push him away too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה carefully. 'Not a firstborn for inheritance' sounds like he still inherits as a regular son. It then challenges this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither family can be sure he belongs to them. Each family can say: 'Prove you are our father's son.' If both families can turn him away, he should get no share at all, so the משנה's implied ruling looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Inheritance
An ordinary son, not the firstborn
He takes
And he will push him away, rejecting his claim

steps.confusionAlert: The question here is not about the double portion of a בכור. It asks how he can get even a regular son's share, since neither family can be forced to accept him.

phrases.english: It is as a firstborn for inheritance that he is not,
but like an ordinary son he takes.
phrases.notes: This is an inference from the wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: But why?
Let him go to this one, and he will push him away,
phrases.notes: The heirs of the first husband.

phrases.english: and to that one, and he will push him away!
phrases.notes: The heirs of the second husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה just quoted and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that the son of uncertain fatherhood inherits a regular share.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person with a doubtful claim against two estates can be turned away by each estate. So he should get nothing from either.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: 'not a firstborn for inheritance' refers to the next son
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rereads the משנה. The words about inheritance describe the second husband's next son, not the son of uncertain fatherhood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: This was needed only for the son who comes after him. This is what the משנה means: the son of uncertain fatherhood is a firstborn for the כהן, and the son who comes after him is not a firstborn for inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers by splitting the משנה's sentence between two different sons. With this reading, the משנה never said the son of uncertain fatherhood inherits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son of uncertain fatherhood may really be the second husband's firstborn. If so, the son born to the second husband afterward cannot claim the double portion of a בכור. The original inference from Step 9 falls away, because the inheritance clause is about a different person.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer
It was needed only for...
The one who comes after him, meaning the next son of the second husband
And this is what it is saying, introducing a new reading of a text

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question. Exactly one of these two sons must be the second husband's real בכור, so the idea of the two sons combining their claims becomes possible.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It was needed only for the one who comes after him,
and this is what it is saying:
he is a firstborn for the כהן,
phrases.notes: This refers to the son of uncertain fatherhood.

phrases.english: and the one who comes after him is not a firstborn for inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the clause is moved to a different subject (אוקימתא of the wording)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole sentence described the son of uncertain fatherhood, so it suggested he inherits a regular share.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the redemption clause refers to the son of uncertain fatherhood. The inheritance clause refers to the second husband's next son, who loses his double portion because of the doubt.

steps.title: Why not have the two sons give each other authorization?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two sons cannot write a הרשאה to each other and claim the double portion together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them write an authorization to each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה's ruling that the next son loses the double portion. It suggests a simple way for the two sons to collect it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the two sons must be the second husband's בכור. If each one signs over his rights to the other, then whoever is the real בכור, the pair together can demand the double portion from the other brothers. So the doubt should not cost them the double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: A power of attorney: a document letting someone collect a claim for you
To each other

phrases.english: And let them write an authorization to each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the next son is 'not a firstborn for inheritance.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One of the two is certainly the בכור. Through a mutual הרשאה, they can jointly claim the double portion, so the doubt should not block it.

steps.title: Blocking the answer that the משנה has no authorization
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out answering that the משנה is a case without a הרשאה, because later the משנה is explained as a case with one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that our משנה is a case without authorization, we explain it later on as a case with authorization!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects the easy answer, 'the משנה is a case where they did not write a הרשאה,' and rejects it right away. The question from Step 11 still needs an answer, and Step 13 gives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A later discussion (on 49a) explains this משנה as a case where a הרשאה was written. So the easy answer contradicts how the גמרא itself reads the משנה later. The גמרא will need a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say, introducing a possible answer
Our משנה
We explain it as referring to a specific case
Ahead of us, later on

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not answer the question in Step 11. It shuts down one possible answer, so the question becomes stronger.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
our משנה is without authorization,
but we explain it later on
as a case with authorization!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא of Step 11 by blocking an obvious answer ahead of time.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the possible answer that our משנה deals with a case where no הרשאה was written.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That answer contradicts the גמרא's own later reading, which explains the משנה as a case with a הרשאה.

steps.title: The משנה supports רבי ינאי: no authorization if the sons were never known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers why the two sons cannot write a הרשאה. רבי ינאי teaches that a הרשאה only works if the sons were known before they got mixed up. Here they never were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה supports רבי ינאי, who said: If the sons were first known and later got mixed up, they write a הרשאה to each other. If they were never known and only later got mixed up, they do not write a הרשאה to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 11. It shows that the משנה fits a rule of רבי ינאי about when a הרשאה helps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הרשאה only passes along a right that someone really had. If each son was once known as his father's son, he had a real claim, so the two can join forces. The son of uncertain fatherhood was never known as anyone's son, so neither of them has a claim to pass on, and the הרשאה does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him (this source backs up his view)
A written authorization that lets one person collect on another's behalf
They were recognized (it was known whose son each was)
They became mixed up

steps.whatToRemember: A הרשאה only helps if each son once had a known, real claim. Sons who were never identified cannot fix the problem by authorizing each other.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a הרשאה creates a new right. It only transfers a right a person already had. That is why it fails when the sons were never recognized.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yannai,
as Rabbi Yannai said:
If they were recognized and in the end became mixed up,
they write an authorization to each other.
If they were not recognized and in the end became mixed up,
they do not write an authorization to each other.
phrases.notes: Our case is this second kind. The uncertain son was never known as anyone's son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 11, after Step 12 ruled out an easier answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A legal distinction: a הרשאה works only where the sons were recognized before they were mixed up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two sons could always join their claims with a הרשאה and take the double portion together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since these sons were never recognized, neither has a real claim to transfer, so a הרשאה does not help.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ינאי's rule about mixed-up sons
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that the uncertain son and the son after him get no double portion

steps.title: A miscarriage of a non-baby does not stop the next child from being firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה asks which child is a בכור both for inheritance and for the כהן. It answers that if the mother first miscarried something that was not a real baby, the next child still counts as the בכור for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Which child is a בכור both for inheritance and for the כהן? Suppose a woman miscarried a sac full of water, or full of blood, or full of pieces of flesh. Or she miscarried something shaped like fish, grasshoppers, or crawling creatures. Or she miscarried on the fortieth day. In all these cases, the child who comes after them is a בכור for inheritance and for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists early miscarriages that do not count as a real birth, so the next child is still the בכור in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of בכור. One is the father's first son, who gets a double inheritance. The other is the first child to open the mother's womb, who is redeemed from a כהן. None of the things listed here is a formed baby (before forty days there is no formed baby), so they do not 'use up' either kind of firstborn status.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn for inheritance: the father's first son, who receives a double portion
Firstborn for the כהן: the mother's first child, redeemed for five סלעים
A woman who miscarries
The sac that holds a fetus
Pieces of flesh

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the basic rule: only a real, formed baby uses up firstborn status. Shapeless or very early miscarriages do not count.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Which child is a firstborn
for inheritance and for the priest?
A woman who miscarries a sac full of water,
full of blood, or full of pieces of flesh;
one who miscarries something like fish or grasshoppers,
repulsive creatures or crawling creatures;
and one who miscarries on the fortieth day,
the child who comes after them
is a firstborn for inheritance and for the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miscarriage of something that is not a formed baby does not count as a birth. The next child is a בכור for both inheritance and the כהן.

steps.title: A caesarean baby and the child after him: neither is firstborn
steps.stepSummary: תנא קמא rules that a baby born by caesarean (יוצא דופן) and the child born after him are both not a בכור, for inheritance or for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baby born by caesarean, and the child who comes after him: neither of them is a בכור, not for inheritance and not for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a contrasting case, a caesarean birth. According to תנא קמא, it takes away firstborn status from both children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The caesarean baby did not come out through the womb in the normal way, so he does not count as a firstborn. But he still came first, so the child born after him is not the first child either. As a result, no one in this family gets firstborn status.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born through the side of the body (by caesarean section)
Neither of them is a firstborn

phrases.english: A baby born by caesarean, and the one who comes after him:
neither of them is a firstborn,
not for inheritance and not for the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a contrasting case. Here the first child does affect firstborn status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to תנא קמא, both a caesarean baby and the child after him lose firstborn status, for inheritance and for the כהן.

steps.title: רבי שמעון splits the two kinds of firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees. He says the caesarean baby is the בכור for inheritance, and the next child is the בכור for the כהן and is redeemed for five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The first child is the בכור for inheritance, and the second child is the בכור for the five סלעים given to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with תנא קמא about the caesarean case. He divides the two kinds of firstborn status between the two children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For inheritance, what counts is the father's first son. The caesarean baby is that son, so he gets the double portion. For the כהן, what counts is the first child to open the womb. The second child is the first to come out of the womb normally, so he is redeemed for five סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees here with the first opinion
Five סלעים, the redemption money given to a כהן for a firstborn son

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא says neither child is a בכור. רבי שמעון says the caesarean child is the בכור for inheritance, and the next child is the בכור for the כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The first is a firstborn for inheritance,
and the second is a firstborn for the five sela coins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with תנא קמא's ruling in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The caesarean baby is the בכור for inheritance. The next child, the first to open the womb, is the בכור for redemption from the כהן.

steps.title: Why the caesarean baby is not a בכור in either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains תנא קמא's ruling on the first son, born by caesarean. He is not the בכור for inheritance, because the פסוק requires a real birth (וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ). He is not the בכור for redemption either, because the פסוק requires opening the womb (פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The first son is not the בכור for inheritance, because we need 'and they bore him' (a real birth). He is also not the בכור for the five סלעים, because we need 'opens the womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the reasons behind תנא קמא's ruling from Step 15. It begins with the first son, the one born by caesarean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of בכור has its own פסוק with its own requirement. For inheritance, the פסוק says 'וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ', which means a natural birth, and a caesarean is not called a birth. For redemption, the פסוק says 'פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם', and this baby never passed through the womb's opening.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they bore him [children]'. The inheritance פסוק, which requires a natural birth.
'Opens the womb'. The redemption פסוק, which requires the baby to open the womb.
We require
Five silver coins. The redemption payment given to a כהן for a firstborn son.
Inheritance. Here it means the double portion a בכור receives.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The first son is not [a firstborn] for inheritance:
phrases.notes: The 'first' son here is the caesarean baby.

phrases.english: we require 'and they have borne him'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:15. A caesarean is not called a birth.

phrases.english: for the five sela'im also not:
phrases.notes: This means redemption from a כהן.

phrases.english: we require 'opens the womb.'
phrases.notes: שמות 13:2. He did not open the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's explanation of the משנה quoted in Steps 15–16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A caesarean baby fails both פסוקים: he is not 'born' for inheritance, and he does not 'open the womb' for redemption.

steps.title: Why the son after the caesarean baby is not a בכור either
steps.stepSummary: The second son is not the בכור for inheritance, because he is not 'the first of his strength'. The caesarean son came before him. He is not the בכור for redemption either, because תנא קמא holds that someone who is a בכור in only one way is not a בכור at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second son is not the בכור for inheritance, because we need 'the first of his strength.' He is also not the בכור for the five סלעים, because [the תנא] holds that a בכור for only one matter is not a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the second son, born naturally after the caesarean baby, is also not a בכור for תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For inheritance, the פסוק says 'רֵאשִׁית אוֹנוֹ', meaning the father's very first child. The caesarean son already came before him. For redemption, he did open the womb, but he is not his mother's first child. תנא קמא holds that being a בכור in only one of these two ways is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The first of his strength'. The father's first child, which is required for the inheritance of a בכור.
He holds (his view is)
A firstborn in only one way. Here: he opened the womb but is not the mother's first child.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'firsts'. The second son IS the first to open the womb, but he is NOT the first child born. That is why he is called a בכור 'for only one matter'.

phrases.english: The second is not [a firstborn] for inheritance:
we require 'the first of his strength'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17. The caesarean son came first.

phrases.english: for the five sela'im also not:
he holds: a firstborn for one matter
is not a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining תנא קמא's view by moving from the first son to the second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a בכור for only one matter is not a בכור, so the second son is not redeemed.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון makes the caesarean baby the בכור for inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words in the משנה again. It explains that he follows his own view elsewhere: the word 'תֵּלֵד' ('she bears') includes a caesarean baby. So for him, a caesarean counts as a birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the first is [the בכור] for inheritance, and the second is for the five סלעים. רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, for he said: 'she bears' comes to include a יוצא דופן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון's view. It first explains why he treats the caesarean son as the בכור for inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנא קמא said a caesarean is not a 'birth', so the son fails 'וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ'. רבי שמעון holds elsewhere that 'תֵּלֵד', in the laws of a woman after childbirth, includes a caesarean. So for him a caesarean IS a birth, and the first son meets the inheritance requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (a view he holds elsewhere)
'She bears'. From ויקרא 12:5.
To include
A baby born by caesarean, 'through the wall' of the belly

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: the first is for inheritance,
phrases.notes: The גמרא re-quotes the משנה so it can explain it.

phrases.english: and the second is for the five sela'im.
Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, for he said:
'she bears' comes to include one born by caesarean.
phrases.notes: So for him a caesarean counts as a 'birth'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי שמעון's disagreement with Step 17 about the first son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי שמעון a caesarean counts as a birth, so the caesarean son is the בכור for inheritance.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון makes the second son the בכור for redemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that a בכור in only one way is still a בכור. So the second son, who opened the womb, is redeemed for five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the second is for the five סלעים, because he holds: a בכור for one matter is a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רבי שמעון's ruling, about the son born after the caesarean baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact opposite of תנא קמא in Step 18. Both agree the second son opened the womb but is not the mother's first child. They argue only about whether that one kind of 'firstness' is enough. רבי שמעון says it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Is (considered)

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא and רבי שמעון argue about two points. First, does a caesarean count as a 'birth'? רבי שמעון says yes, based on 'תֵּלֵד'. Second, is a בכור in only one way still a בכור? רבי שמעון says yes. That is why for him the first son inherits as the בכור and the second son is redeemed.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is a general principle. It decides any case where the 'firsts' for the father and for the mother do not match.

phrases.english: And the second is for the five sela'im,
he holds: a firstborn for one matter
is a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining רבי שמעון's view, directly opposite to Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: a בכור for only one matter is a בכור, so the second son is redeemed for five סלעים.
